lab_supply_as_reported: 400 kHz RF generator (30 kW maximum), 17-27 kW; 21-turn coil, L = 25 uH, R = 310 mOhm
electrical_requirement: RF current in an induction coil. Torches have run from 9.6 kHz to 40 MHz at 0.5 kW to ~1 MW (PW055-V05). Coupling needs plasma radius / skin depth of ~1.5-4 (PW055-V02), so the minimum frequency falls roughly as 1/D^2: ~4 MHz for a 40 mm tube, ~0.5 MHz for >=100 mm, a 50 kHz band for >=200 mm (PW058-V02 to -V04). Lower frequency also needs more power to sustain the plasma (~1 MW at 960 Hz in argon, PW055-V04). SRC009: 80 mm tube at 400 kHz
candidate_classes: K2 (solid-state, to ~400 kHz, 50-100 kW units); R1 (tube oscillator, 0.3-3 MHz in the values, 100 kW units); R2 (solid-state RF, 0.3-60 MHz, 1.5-5 kW units)
class_used: SRC009 (400 kHz): R1 and K2 shown
industrial_unit_scale: Solid-state >=95% supplies: >=100 kW at 0-0.5 MHz, ~30 kW at >=1 MHz (PW058-V05, -V06); induction generators 50-100 kW at 100-400 kHz; tube generators for ICP up to 120 kW at 2-3 MHz (PW061-V01); largest ICP facility 1.2 MW at 400 kHz, 160 mm torch (PW056-V01, -V02)
scale_up_constraint: Frequency is set by torch size. A large torch (>=100 mm) runs at <=0.5 MHz, where >=95% solid-state supplies of >=100 kW exist; small torches (<=40 mm) need several MHz, where only tubes (50-60%) or solid-state units of <=~30 kW are available. Scale-up therefore moves an ICP torch into the efficient supply range, the reverse of microwave. For SRC009 the supply choice changes wall-basis EC by ~40%. Coil and matching losses are in neither class; K2 efficiencies are for induction-heating loads
verdict: supply choice matters and depends on torch size; large torches fall in the efficient solid-state range
